title: Living at the last day; whether the impious rise
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Resurrection stands as sometimes taken strictly unto such that unto blessed life. Besides recent Jews plus Socinians, Scripture on ye judge belonging toward living plus dead, eternal fire, plus ye worm such that dies not must be opposed. Next, will ye impious also rise? Both expositions stand. Augustine Retractations 2.33: Either they will not die, or they will not feel death. 4 — by a shortcut belonging toward death through change, ye living will not die but be stripped belonging toward mortality. 15:51 plus 1 Thess. ye Apostle at 1 Cor. Christ stands as judge belonging toward living plus dead; Of those found alive it may be asked whether they will rise, since they have not fallen.
pass_b_english: Of those found alive it may be asked whether they will rise, since they have not fallen. Christ is judge of living and dead; the Apostle at 1 Cor. 15:51 and 1 Thess. 4 — by a shortcut of death through change, the living will not die but be stripped of mortality. Augustine Retractations 2.33: Either they will not die, or they will not feel death. Both expositions stand. Next, will the impious also rise? Besides recent Jews and Socinians, Scripture on the judge of living and dead, eternal fire, and the worm that dies not must be opposed. Resurrection is sometimes taken strictly for that unto blessed life.
source_text: De iis qui vivi offenduntur quaeri potest an sint resurrecturi, cum non ceciderint. Christus judex vivorum & mortuorum; Apostolus 1 Cor. 15.51 & 1 Thess. 4 — per demutationem mortis compendio, vivi non morituri sed mortalitate exuendi. Augustinus Retract. 2.33: Aut non morientur, aut mortem non sentient. Utraque expositio consistit. Deinde an etiam impii sint resurrecturi? Praeter recentiores Judaeos & Socinianos, opponi debent scripturae de judice vivorum & mortuorum, igne aeterno, verme qui non moritur. Resurrectio interdum stricte pro ea ad vitam beatam sumitur.
